overview: Multi-site qualitative study at five hospitals, February to May 2027, with staff interviews and structured observation of day and night shifts, coded with CFIR and compared between higher- and lower-performing sites.
population: Emergency nurses and physicians, ward nurses, junior doctors on call, pharmacists and managers involved in sepsis care at the five hospitals; night-shift and agency staff included.
exposure: Not applicable; the phenomenon of interest is how the sepsis bundle is delivered at each site.
procedures: Sites ranked by twelve months of network time-to-antibiotics figures and recording practice checked; about 8 to 10 interviews per site by purposive sampling across professions and shifts; two structured observation shifts per site, one at night; interviews audio-recorded with consent and summarised within 48 hours using a structured template.

outcomes.name: Determinants of one-hour antibiotic delivery
outcomes.measure: CFIR constructs coded from interviews and observation, each rated for valence and strength by site
outcomes.why: What an implementation strategy should target.

outcomes.name: Contrast between higher- and lower-performing sites
outcomes.measure: Constructs whose ratings distinguish the two highest- and two lowest-performing sites
outcomes.why: Explains the variation the investigator described.

outcomes.name: Sample coverage
outcomes.measure: Interviews completed by profession, site and shift, including night-shift staff at every site
outcomes.why: Night care is the known gap.

feasibility: About 34 fieldwork days from one research nurse two days a week over four months cover 40 to 50 interviews and 10 observation shifts; transcription is replaced by structured summaries and selective transcription.
biasMitigation: Site performance withheld from coders until constructs are rated
Double coding of 20 percent of interviews
Interviewer not employed at the site being studied

biasFlags.label: Social desirability
biasFlags.note: Staff may describe the bundle as intended rather than as done; observation checks accounts.

flags: No patient-level outcome data; the question is explanatory
parsimony.simplestPath: Five sites, one framework, one contrast.

theoreticalFramework: CFIR, because the question is about determinants of implementation across settings; no second framework.
summary: Five-site qualitative study with CFIR coding, day and night observation, and a high-low performer contrast.
